A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 19-page versions of the same FineVD/FineVQ study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original FineVD annotation results from 22 subjects and FineVQ quality-prediction, cross-dataset and ablation experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds runtime and throughput measurements in Table 7.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same spatial/motion encoders, InternLM backbone, projectors, instruction tuning, LoRA adaptation and combined language/L1 loss. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: FineVD's 6104 videos, quality-assessment tasks and external UGC benchmarks remain unchanged. The added timing sample introduces evaluation settings without identifying a new dataset, domain or prediction task.

E2.justification: The predictive comparisons retain their comparator sets. V2's runtime Table 7 uses the same eleven IQA/VQA baselines already evaluated in Table 1.

E3.justification: V2 adds runtime and FPS evaluation on ten 2K videos containing 240 frames each, using an A6000 card or MATLAB. Existing predictive-evaluation splits, metrics and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 adds a computational-efficiency analysis comparing FineVQ's runtime and throughput with baselines. Existing motion/LoRA ablations and Appendix D's frame-count and instruction-tuning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Subjective-rating variability, outlier procedures and multi-round validation descriptions are unchanged. The runtime addition provides point estimates without new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance-test reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports FineVQ at 18.57 seconds and 129.3 FPS, versus FastVQA at 13.12 seconds/182.9 FPS and DOVER at 9.006 seconds/266.5 FPS. Existing quality-prediction, cross-dataset and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The Z-score/MOS calculations, LoRA formulation and loss equations (1–8), including the appendix mathematics, are unchanged in substance. No new assumptions, derivations or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: FineVD, unified fine-grained assessment through FineVQ, and claimed state-of-the-art predictive performance. The runtime addition does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Explanations of temporal weaknesses, generalization, distortion relationships and adaptation remain unchanged. The added statement of comparable runtime summarizes the new measurements without introducing a substantive mechanism explanation, applicability qualification or limitation.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the future-release promise with a repository link and a statement that FineVD and FineVQ are publicly available. It also documents the timing-test setup; implementation details for the retained model and training remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds the citation 'Develop then rival: A human vision-inspired framework for superimposed image decomposition' to the introduction's motivation. Broader research positioning is retained; other reference-number shifts reflect this addition.

P1.justification: V2 adds author contact and corresponding-author information, an acknowledgment and brief runtime prose, alongside small wording corrections such as IternLM to InternLM. The narrative and section order remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds runtime Table 7, resizes or repositions existing figures and reflows the main text, including moving Figure 4 to the left column. Appendix Tables 7–9 become Tables 8–10 with unchanged content.

improvement.justification: The runtime comparison and concrete resource-access link modestly improve practical assessment and reproducibility information. Predictive evidence remains unchanged. The sparse 'A6000 card or MATLAB' description leaves execution conditions for individual baselines unclear, limiting the strength of the efficiency comparison.
